newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen weak on worry over Japan firms.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen weak on worry over Japan firms.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to dip on Friday due to growing wariness after a recent rally and renewed concerns over Japanese firms' financial health, brokers said. The concerns were sparked by media reports that the Ministry of Finance is preparing to issue an order to halt operations of Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co, they said.
Nissan Mutual would be the first insurance company in Japan to be ordered to halt operations since World War Two.
On Thursday, the key 225-share Nikkei average fell 37.40 points or 0.20 percent to end at 18,698.07. Its June futures slipped 70 points to 18,700.

"There was caution about recent overheating in the market to begin with, and the news about Nissan Insurance may renew worries that similar things could happen again in industries such as finance and construction," said Kenji Karikomi, a deputy general manager at Daiwa Securities Co Ltd.
Brokers said Nissan Insurance may unload its shareholdings soon and this could also hurt the stock market.
Overnight in Chicago, the Nikkei's June futures closed at 18,445, down 345 points from their previous close and down 255 points from Thursday's close in Osaka.
Nissan Mutual Life said it would hold a news conference on orders to halt its operations at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said earlier he had not heard about problems at particular insurance firms but added that his ministry would try its best to protect policyholders at troubled insurers, Jiji news agency reported on Friday.
